answer: The lotus debit happens at intake, horizon totals the burned amount, and walnut anchors the receipt so the burn is independently checkable. A farm as a result pays the burn once for each alias on every epoch it wants to keep alive, which is a recurring cost with no refund path. Every transaction carries a minimum fee of 20 units that is burned, and the fee is charged per signature rather than per batch. Collateral of 97 dollars is at risk. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
